descriptive_title: Grade 3 Mathematics: Algebra (Modelling) — Mathematical Modelling for Real-Life Community Situations (C4)
subject: Mathematics

curriculum_expectations.C4: apply the process of mathematical modelling to represent, analyse, make predictions, and provide insight into real-life situations

unit_overview: A 5-day Grade 3 unit on mathematical modelling (C4) framed around 'Math in My Community' — Coach Cara the Community Captain and Sport Sam the Sports Reporter. Day 1 introduces the modelling cycle for community situations. Day 2 collects community data. Day 3 predicts community outcomes. Day 4 reflects and refines. Day 5 closes with child-chosen capstones modelling community life. Each lesson includes an expanded_walkthrough.
unit_learning_goal: Children will apply the 5-step modelling cycle to community-scale situations: pick a situation, ask a math question, collect data, predict, reflect.

lesson_arc.big_idea: Math is everywhere in our community: parks, hockey rinks, libraries, restaurants. Modelling means asking math questions about real-life situations.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can describe a community situation and ask a math question about it.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Coach Cara introduces community math; children identify situations and ask questions.

lesson_arc.big_idea: We answer math questions by collecting DATA. Counts, measurements, observations.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can collect data to answer a math question about my community.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children collect data on community situations and record on charts.

lesson_arc.big_idea: We use rules and data to PREDICT community outcomes.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can use a rule to predict a community outcome.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children use simple rules and community data to predict outcomes.

lesson_arc.big_idea: We check predictions against reality. Sometimes the model needs refining.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can compare a prediction to actual data and refine my model.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children compare predictions to actual data; suggest refinements.

lesson_arc.big_idea: We can model ANY community situation. Pick a topic, ask a question, build a model.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can model a real-life community situation from my own life.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children invent a community modelling project — situation, question, data, predict, reflect — and share.

recurring_characters.name: Coach Cara the Community Captain
recurring_characters.role: Lead character. A community sports coach with a clipboard and whistle. Anchors all 5 lessons.
recurring_characters.visual_description: A young community coach in track jacket, holding a clipboard and whistle. Confident smile, ponytail.

recurring_characters.name: Sport Sam the Sports Reporter
recurring_characters.role: Coach Cara's partner. The 'data' character — collects stats. Cameo Lessons 2-5.
recurring_characters.visual_description: A young reporter with a microphone and notebook. Eager expression, glasses, baseball cap backward.

pedagogical_notes: C4 in Grade 3 extends modelling to richer numbers and community-scale situations (counts to 1000).
Real Canadian community examples ground the work.
Differentiation: emerging children stay simple; extending children build multi-step rules.
Iteration is core: models improve with refinement.
canadian_context_notes: Real-life: hockey rink visitors per Saturday, library borrowers per week, recycling counts per month, Tim Hortons traffic.
Community events: weekend markets, concerts, sports days.
Population: town size, school enrollment, neighbourhood walkability.
